project.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

parsed_output.evidence: Ran `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` inside the project container. Output: "[POV] escaped target : /workspace/repo/target/pov-zipslip/pov_pwned.txt exists=true", "[POV] confined target : .../dest/pov_pwned.txt exists=false", "[POV] VULNERABLE: zip entry escaped the destination directory (Zip Slip)." with EXIT=0. Source confirms UnzipEngine.getOutputFileNameWithPath (line 446) returns `outPath + System.getProperty("file.separator") + fileName` and getOutputStream (line 422/432) builds the File and FileOutputStream directly from it.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: ZipFile.extractAll() writes the archive entry named "../pov_pwned.txt" to the parent of the destination directory (target/pov-zipslip/pov_pwned.txt instead of target/pov-zipslip/dest/pov_pwned.txt), so the escaped target file exists and the POV exits 0. A correct patch validates the resolved canonical output path stays within the destination (throwing or refusing to write), so the escaped file is never created and the POV exits 1.
parsed_output.notes: POV files live under .security-pipeline/pov/ only; no product code or tests were modified. The malicious archive is built with java.util.zip.ZipOutputStream (JDK-only, no extra deps) so the traversal entry name is preserved, then extracted through zip4j's real public API (net.lingala.zip4j.core.ZipFile.extractAll). run_pov.sh recompiles product source via `mvn -B -DskipTests compile` before each run so it always tests current (patched or unpatched) code. Command must be run inside /workspace/repo in the project container (via the provided run_in_docker.sh wrapper on the host).
parsed_output.regression_hint: After patching, the same command `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` should exit non-zero: the traversal entry "../pov_pwned.txt" must not be written outside the destination directory (extraction should throw a ZipException or normalize/reject the entry). Confirm target/pov-zipslip/pov_pwned.txt is NOT created.
parsed_output.summary: Created a real Zip Slip (CWE-022) POV. zip4j's UnzipEngine.getOutputFileNameWithPath() concatenates the extraction directory with the archive entry name (outPath + separator + fileName) with no path-traversal sanitization. The POV crafts a malicious zip whose entry name is "../pov_pwned.txt", extracts it via the public ZipFile.extractAll() API, and confirms the file is written OUTSIDE the intended destination directory. It exits 0 on the vulnerable (unpatched) code and is designed to exit non-zero once a correct patch confines extraction to the destination.

parsed_output.patch_notes: In UnzipEngine.getOutputStream(), after building the target File from getOutputFileNameWithPath(outPath, newFileName), added a call to a new helper assertFileWithinDestination(file, new File(outPath)). The helper compares canonical paths: it computes the canonical path of the destination directory and the target file, and throws a ZipException ("illegal file name that breaks out of the target directory: ...") unless the file's canonical path equals the destination or starts with the destination path plus File.separator. The separator suffix check prevents a sibling directory sharing a name prefix (e.g. /dest vs /destination) from being treated as inside the destination. This blocks entry names containing "../" traversal sequences from escaping the extraction root. The check is placed before any mkdirs()/delete()/FileOutputStream operations so no side effects occur for malicious entries. No imports were added (java.io.File/IOException/ZipException already imported); no dependencies changed. Verified inside the project container: mvn compile + POV now reports "NOT VULNERABLE" and exits 1 (escaped target file not created), the confined path is likewise absent because extraction aborts on the malicious entry, and mvn -B test and mvn -B -DskipTests package both succeed.
parsed_output.risk_notes: Behavioral change: entries that resolve outside the destination directory now cause extraction to throw a ZipException rather than silently writing outside it — this is the intended security behavior but could surface as an error for archives that legitimately relied on absolute/traversal paths (rare and itself unsafe). Uses File.getCanonicalPath(), which resolves symlinks and may perform filesystem access; for non-existent parents it still resolves lexically/relative to CWD correctly. The project has no existing test framework (no JUnit dependency, no src/test tree), so no unit test was added to avoid introducing new dependencies; the separately-run POV plus the build command serve as regression verification.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed the Zip Slip / path traversal (CWE-022) in net.lingala.zip4j.unzip.UnzipEngine by validating the canonical resolved output path stays within the extraction destination directory before creating/writing the file. Malicious entries like "../pov_pwned.txt" now throw a ZipException instead of being written outside the destination.

parsed_output.diff_review: Only product change is in src/main/java/net/lingala/zip4j/unzip/UnzipEngine.java: a new private helper assertFileWithinDestination(file, new File(outPath)) is invoked at line 424, immediately after the target File is built (line 422) and before parent mkdirs (426), existing-file delete (431), and FileOutputStream creation (434) — so no filesystem side effects occur for a malicious entry. The helper compares File.getCanonicalPath() of the destination and target, allows only when the file equals the dest or starts with dest + File.separator, and correctly guards against prefix-sibling directories (e.g. /dest vs /destination). It throws ZipException on traversal and wraps IOException as ZipException. No new imports/dependencies. The sink at getOutputFileNameWithPath (line 475, unchanged) still concatenates naively, but the new guard neutralizes the traversal at the write point. Remaining diff hunks are POV files under .security-pipeline/pov/ (not product code) and generated target/ maven build artifacts (not source). POV itself is unmodified by the patch.
parsed_output.pov_result: Reran `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` via the Docker wrapper: extractAll now throws ZipException ("illegal file name that breaks out of the target directory"), escaped target exists=false, confined target exists=false, prints "NOT VULNERABLE", POV_EXIT=1. Before patch the orchestrator log shows exit 0 (escaped file written). Vulnerability no longer reproduces.
parsed_output.regression_result: `mvn -B test` inside the container: BUILD SUCCESS (project has no test sources — "No tests to run"). `mvn -B -DskipTests package` in orchestrator log also BUILD SUCCESS. Compilation of the patched source succeeds. Legitimate entries resolve within the destination and pass the startsWith(dest+separator) check, so normal extraction is unaffected.
parsed_output.summary: The patch fixes the Zip Slip / path-traversal vulnerability (CWE-022) in UnzipEngine.getOutputStream() by validating the canonical resolved output path against the canonical destination directory before any mkdirs/delete/FileOutputStream side effect. Malicious entries like "../pov_pwned.txt" now throw a ZipException. Independently reran the POV (exits 1, NOT VULNERABLE, no escaped file) and the regression build/test (BUILD SUCCESS). Diff is minimal, appropriate, and does not touch the POV or disable functionality.
